summary: Pure Elixir engine for Barkpark's PortableDoc block format: immutable patch operations over a block tree, dual-target HTML rendering (email and article), bound/free block projection onto document fields, and a legacy block-list synthesizer. Together these modules form the server-side document processing core that powers Papers (Bulldocs), the Studio editor View pane, and email export.

intentions.title: Maintain a cross-process, cross-language PortableDoc contract
intentions.evidence: patch.ex explicitly ports TS applyDocPatch() and references a shared inter-repo contract (docs/doc-patch-op-contract.md) and golden fixtures. render.ex calls itself 'a direct in-process port of the TS walk() in portable-doc/packages/backend-web'. Both modules operate on string-keyed maps (the JSON wire shape) to stay byte-compatible with TypeScript consumers.

intentions.title: Provide a pure, immutable, all-or-nothing patch engine for block trees
intentions.evidence: patch.ex apply_patch/2 and apply_patches/2 are stateless (no Repo, no GenServer, no I/O), return structured errors on the first failure, never partially-apply a batch, and rebuild only the changed path (structural sharing). Six ops cover insert, append, patch, replace, remove, and move.

intentions.title: Render rich document content to HTML for both email and article surfaces without a Node sidecar
intentions.evidence: render.ex declares 'NO React, NO JSX, NO Node sidecar'. Two palettes (email, article) diverge on typography, semantics (PdHeading vs bold span, PdParagraph vs PdText, PdList vs flex-row scaffold), and CSS variable vs hardcoded-hex colour — email stays byte-stable for Outlook; article uses CSS variables that flip with the Studio dark-mode theme.

intentions.title: Project field-block values onto document content keys on every write (no-drift guarantee)
intentions.evidence: projection.ex bound/free partition writes content[fieldName] and content['body'] on every block op or upsert, declared as the SOLE writer of those keys. Existing Classic queries read content[fieldName] unchanged — the projection is a backwards-compatible derived index.

intentions.title: Support paperflow-native article typography (serif body, parchment palette, Mermaid figures, asciicast embeds)
intentions.evidence: render.ex article_palette uses Iowan Old Style / Georgia serif stack and CSS variable warm-parchment colours. Dedicated compose_block clauses for diagram, asciicast, figure, divider, code, eyebrow, byline, ingress emit article-mode HTML that mirrors doc.css visual conventions; email mode degrades gracefully.

intentions.title: Enforce XSS safety at the renderer boundary with a strict URL allowlist and HTML escaping
intentions.evidence: render.ex safe_url/1 restricts href/src to https?/mailto/tel schemes; safe_hex/1 validates color values before they reach inline styles; escape_html/1 is called on all user strings; the _raw escape hatch is used only for internally-generated HTML (diagram, code, form blocks), never for user content.

intentions.title: Render structured field blocks (composite, arrayOf, codelist, localizedText) as human-readable View output
intentions.evidence: render.ex has compose_block clauses for field-string, field-boolean, field-select, field-datetime, field-color, field-reference, field-image, composite, arrayOf, codelist, localizedText — each produces a labelled PdBox(column) row. ref_resolver and codelist_resolver injected via opts keep the renderer pure while enabling title and label resolution.
